root_cause.text: The vt alternate-screen code in `leave_alt_screen()` unconditionally restored `vc_saved_uni_lines` even after a resize, so the unicode screen buffer allocated for the old `vc_rows`/`vc_cols` was reused with new dimensions and later indexed out of bounds.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explains that `enter_alt_screen()` saves `vc_uni_lines` into `vc_saved_uni_lines`, `vc_do_resize()` skips reallocating when `vc_uni_lines` is NULL, and `leave_alt_screen()` then restores the stale buffer; the fix adds a `uni_lines_stale` check comparing `vc_saved_rows/cols` against `vc_rows/cols` and frees `vc->vc_saved_uni_lines` instead of restoring it when they differ.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add local state needed for upcoming handling of stale Unicode line information when restoring the normal screen.
intent_record.what: A new local boolean variable named `uni_lines_stale` was added to `leave_alt_screen(struct vc_data *vc)` alongside the existing `rows`, `cols`, `src`, and `dest` declarations.
intent_record.how: This change only introduces a variable declaration in the shown hunk; by itself it does not alter runtime behavior, but it likely prepares the function to track whether Unicode line state needs refreshing when leaving the alternate screen.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid restoring stale alternate-screen unicode state after a console resize to prevent out-of-bounds access.
intent_record.what: The code in leave_alt_screen() was changed from always calling vc_uniscr_set(vc, vc->vc_saved_uni_lines) to first checking whether the console size changed while in the alternate screen. It now computes uni_lines_stale by comparing vc_saved_rows/cols against vc_rows/cols, frees vc->vc_saved_uni_lines with vc_uniscr_free() when stale, and only restores it with vc_uniscr_set() when the saved dimensions still match. The comment block explaining the resize case was added, while vc->vc_saved_uni_lines is still set to NULL afterward.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the kernel from reusing a unicode screen buffer that was allocated for an old console geometry after a resize. If the screen was resized in alternate mode, the saved unicode line data is discarded instead of being restored, avoiding out-of-bounds accesses and letting the unicode screen state be rebuilt safely later.

This directly addresses the root cause described for `leave_alt_screen()` unconditionally reusing the old unicode buffer after resize.
